sections.title: 1. ABOUT THESE TERMS
2. DEFINITIONS
sections.content:
For purposes of these Terms:
“Account” means any Nordi Remitwave account, payment account, wallet, profile, investment account, credit account or other account made available to you.
“AI System” means any machine - learning, generative - AI, predictive, classification, scoring, recommendation, natural - language, fraud - detection, risk - analysis or other automated computational system used in connection with the Services.
“Applicable Law” means all laws, regulations, regulatory rules, codes, licence conditions, court orders, sanctions programs, financial - crime requirements and binding regulatory directions applicable to the relevant Service, Company entity, transaction or customer.
“Business Day” means a day on which the relevant financial institutions, payment systems or markets necessary to process the applicable transaction are open, excluding weekends and public holidays where appropriate.
“Digital Asset” means a cryptoasset, virtual asset, cryptographic token, stablecoin, tokenized asset, digital security, utility token, governance token, non - fungible token or other blockchain - recorded representation of value, rights or interests.
“Fiat Currency” means government - issued currency that is legal tender in the relevant jurisdiction.
“Partner” means a bank, payment processor, card network, broker, custodian, lender, investment manager, liquidity provider, exchange, digital - asset custodian, identity - verification provider, blockchain analytics provider, credit bureau, insurer, cloud provider or other third party involved in providing a Service.
“Restricted Jurisdiction” means any country, region, territory or location in which we prohibit or limit Services because of Applicable Law, sanctions, licensing restrictions, fraud or financial - crime risk, commercial risk, or Partner requirements.
“User,” “you,” and “your” mean the person or legal entity that accesses or uses the Services.

sections.title: 3. CONTRACTING ENTITY AND REGULATORY CAPACITY
sections.content:

Nordi Remitwave may operate through multiple affiliated legal entities.The entity providing a Service may differ depending on:
- your country of residence or incorporation;
- the type of Service;
- the currency, asset or payment rail involved;
- licensing and regulatory requirements;
- whether a Partner provides the regulated component; and
- changes to our corporate or regulatory structure.
The applicable contracting or regulated entity will be identified in your onboarding flow, Product Schedule, transaction confirmation or other legally required disclosure.
3.2 No implied licence or status
The Nordi Remitwave brand does not itself mean that every entity using the brand is a bank, insured depository institution, broker-dealer, investment adviser, securities exchange, lender, money transmitter, payment institution, electronic - money institution, cryptoasset service provider, virtual - asset service provider, custodian or other regulated financial institution.
A particular Service is regulated only to the extent stated in the relevant Product Schedule and only under the identified entity’s applicable licence, registration, authorization or exemption.
3.3 Partner - provided regulated services
Where a Service is legally provided by a Partner, Nordi Remitwave may act as a technology provider, program manager, distributor, agent, intermediary, introducer or outsourced service provider.Your legal relationship for the regulated service may therefore also be governed by the Partner’s terms.
3.4 No evasion of local law
Nothing in these Terms authorizes any activity that would be unlawful in your jurisdiction.We may refuse, restrict, geofence or discontinue a Service where providing it would require a licence, registration or approval that is unavailable, has not been obtained or no longer applies.

sections.title: 12. BANKING, DEPOSIT - LIKE AND STORED - VALUE SERVICES
sections.content:
12.1 Nature of funds
The legal treatment of fiat balances depends on the product and jurisdiction.A balance may constitute:
- a deposit with a licensed bank;
- safeguarded customer funds;
- electronic money;
- stored value;
- funds held in a custodial or pooled account;
- money held by a payment institution; or
- another legally recognized form of customer funds.
The applicable Product Schedule will explain the legal structure.
12.2 Deposit insurance
Funds are not covered by deposit insurance, compensation schemes or government guarantees unless a Product Schedule expressly states that they are and identifies the applicable scheme, limits and eligibility conditions.
12.3 Safeguarding is not deposit insurance
Where customer funds are safeguarded or segregated, safeguarding does not necessarily provide the same legal protection as deposit insurance.Recovery may be delayed and may be affected by insolvency, reconciliation, third - party costs or applicable insolvency law.
12.4 Interest
Interest is payable only where expressly stated.Interest rates may be variable and may change subject to Applicable Law and required notice.
12.5 Negative balances
You must repay any negative Account balance, overdraft or amount owed to us when due.We may offset amounts as permitted by law and by the relevant Product Schedule.

sections.title: PRODUCT SCHEDULE A — GLOBAL PAYMENTS AND REMITTANCES
sections.content:
This Schedule applies where Nordi Remitwave provides or arranges domestic or international payments or remittances.
A1.Pre - transaction disclosures
Where required, before you commit to a remittance we will disclose the amount to be transferred, applicable fees, exchange rate or methodology, expected amount to be received, estimated availability and legally required cancellation or error - resolution information.
A2.Recipient responsibility
You are responsible for selecting the intended recipient and verifying beneficiary information.We may use confirmation - of - payee, account - name matching or similar services where available, but such tools may not be conclusive.
A3.Cancellation and refunds
Consumer remittance cancellation rights, cooling - off rights and refund requirements imposed by law apply and override inconsistent contractual language.
A4.Correspondent banking
Cross - border payments may use correspondent banks and intermediary institutions.Such institutions may conduct their own compliance screening and may reject or delay transactions.
A5.Restricted corridors
We may open, limit or close payment corridors based on licensing, sanctions, Partner availability, fraud risk, foreign - exchange controls or regulatory requirements.

sections.title: PRODUCT SCHEDULE B — CREDIT AND LOANS
sections.content:
This Schedule applies to loans, lines of credit, overdrafts, installment financing and similar credit products.
B1.Contract hierarchy
The specific credit agreement controls pricing, repayments, default, security and other economic terms.
B2.Regulatory disclosures
We will provide standardized pre - contract and post - contract disclosures where required, including APR or equivalent information, total cost, repayment schedule and statutory notices.
B3.Affordability and responsible lending
We may decline or reduce credit where affordability, responsible - lending, prudential or fraud controls require it.
B4.Automated underwriting
Automated or AI - assisted underwriting may be used only subject to applicable fair - lending, explainability, adverse - action and human - review requirements.
B5.Early repayment
Where you have a statutory or contractual right to prepay, the applicable agreement will describe any lawful rebate, fee or calculation.
B6.Hardship
Where required by law or offered by policy, customers experiencing financial difficulty may request hardship assistance, restructuring, forbearance or another available accommodation.

C3.Custody

C4.Fractional interests
Fractional investment interests may have limited voting, transfer, corporate - action and marketability rights.
C5.Advice
Where personalized advice is provided, the responsible licensed entity and scope of advisory duty will be identified.
C6.Algorithmic recommendations
Algorithms may rebalance or recommend portfolios based on disclosed assumptions and customer profile information.Customers must keep profile information current.

sections.title: PRODUCT SCHEDULE D — DIGITAL ASSETS AND BLOCKCHAIN
sections.content:

D2.Custody

D3.Withdrawals

D4.Delisting
We may suspend trading or support for a Digital Asset because of legal, security, liquidity, market - integrity, technology or Partner concerns.Where practicable and lawful, we will provide a withdrawal or conversion window.
D5.Protocol events
Treatment of forks, airdrops, staking rewards and protocol migrations is at our reasonable discretion subject to Applicable Law and disclosed policies.

E5.Safety controls

ANNEX 1 — MANDATORY CUSTOMER RISK DISCLOSURES
sections.content:
1. General financial risk
Financial products can result in loss.Fees, taxes, market movements, credit events, exchange rates and operational events may reduce value.
2. Credit risk
Borrowing creates a repayment obligation.Failure to repay may result in fees, collection activity, enforcement of security and negative credit reporting where lawful.
3. Investment risk
Investment values fluctuate.You may receive less than you invested or lose the entire investment.
4. Digital Asset risk
Digital Assets are highly risky and may lose all value.Legal protection, compensation schemes, liquidity and custody protections may be materially different from traditional financial products.
5. Stablecoin risk
Stablecoins may depeg or fail.Redemption rights depend on the issuer, reserve structure, liquidity and applicable law.
6. Smart - contract risk
Smart contracts may contain bugs, exploits or unexpected logic and may be difficult or impossible to reverse.
7. AI risk
AI outputs can be wrong.AI - generated forecasts, recommendations or summaries should not be treated as guarantees.
8. Foreign - exchange risk
Exchange rates fluctuate and may change the value or cost of a transaction.
9. Counterparty risk
Banks, brokers, custodians, liquidity providers, issuers and other counterparties may fail or become insolvent.
10. Technology risk
Cyber incidents, outages, compromised credentials and infrastructure failures may interrupt access or cause loss.
